note: Fabric guide. level: 1 = great for beginners, 2 = needs a little care, 3 = tricky. weave: plain, twill, satin, knit, rib, pile, gauze, crinkle (used for the little swatch drawing).

fabrics.name: Quilting cotton
fabrics.about: The friendly, stable cotton sold in endless prints. It presses beautifully and holds a crease, which makes it the best fabric to learn on.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash warm and tumble dry. Expect it to shrink 3–5%.
tips: Too stiff for flowy clothes: it stands away from the body.
Check the print direction before cutting: some prints only go one way.

fabrics.name: Cotton poplin
fabrics.stretch: None, or a little if it has spandex
fabrics.about: A tightly woven, smooth cotton with a slight sheen. Classic for shirts because it's crisp, cool, and easy to press.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry as you'll wash the garment.
tips: Shows needle holes, so unpick carefully.
A fresh, sharp needle keeps seams from puckering.

fabrics.name: Cotton lawn
fabrics.about: A fine, smooth, lightweight cotton with a silky hand. Lovely for summer clothes; a bit see-through in pale colors.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash gentle, then dry.
tips: French seams look neat on the inside of sheer fabric.
Hold the thread tails as you start so the fabric isn't pulled into the needle hole.

fabrics.name: Voile
fabrics.about: Very light and semi-sheer, a little looser than lawn. Breezy and cool.
fabrics.prewash: Hand or machine wash gentle.
tips: Use French seams or very narrow finished seams.
Starch spray makes it much easier to cut.

fabrics.name: Chambray
fabrics.about: Looks like light denim: a colored thread one way and white the other. Plain weave, so it's lighter and softer than denim.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry. Wash dark chambray alone the first time.
tips: The two sides often look different: pick one and stay with it.

fabrics.name: Oxford shirting
fabrics.about: A soft but sturdy shirting with a tiny basket-like texture, made with paired threads. A classic for casual button-ups.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry.
tips: Easy to topstitch neatly, which makes it great for a first shirt.

fabrics.name: Denim
fabrics.stretch: None, or some if it's stretch denim
fabrics.about: A sturdy twill with diagonal lines, usually a blue thread one way and white the other. Weights run from light shirting denim to heavy jeans denim.
fabrics.prewash: Wash and dry hot, twice for raw denim. It can shrink 5–10%.
tips: Use a hammer or a seam ripper's back to flatten bulky seam crossings before sewing over them.
Topstitching thread looks classic, but needs a bigger needle (100/16 or a topstitch needle).
Stretch denim needs the stretch going around the body.

fabrics.name: Canvas and duck
fabrics.about: Thick, tightly woven, and tough. Duck is a smoother, tighter canvas. Great for things that need to stand up and wear well.
fabrics.press: Hot, with steam and a firm press
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry if the finished thing will be washed. It shrinks.
tips: Clips hold layers better than pins.
Go slowly over thick seams, turning the handwheel by hand if needed.

fabrics.name: Cotton twill and drill
fabrics.stretch: None, or a little with spandex
fabrics.about: Sturdy with a fine diagonal rib, like chinos. Drill is a heavier twill. Wears well and hides wrinkles.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry.
tips: The diagonal lines run the same way on every piece if you cut them all the same way up.

fabrics.name: Corduroy
fabrics.stretch: None, or a little with spandex
fabrics.about: A woven fabric with soft raised ribs called wales. Fine-wale is thin; wide-wale is chunky. It has a nap, so it looks different up and down.
fabrics.press: Medium, from the wrong side, on a fluffy towel so the ribs don't flatten
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash inside out, tumble dry.
tips: Cut every piece with the nap going the same way (a 'with nap' layout).
A walking foot stops the layers creeping.

fabrics.name: Cotton flannel
fabrics.about: Brushed so it's fuzzy and warm. Cozy and forgiving, though it frays and sheds a little lint.
fabrics.prewash: Wash and dry hot. It can shrink a lot, so prewash twice.
tips: Finish every seam: flannel frays.
Clean the lint out of your bobbin area after sewing.

fabrics.name: Double gauze
fabrics.about: Two layers of loose, airy gauze tacked together. Soft, breathable, and lovely once washed, though it frays and shifts.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry. Expect it to shrink and crinkle a bit.
tips: Flat-felled or French seams keep the fraying hidden.
Don't stretch it while cutting: it grows.

fabrics.name: Seersucker
fabrics.about: Woven with puckered stripes, so it stands off the skin and stays cool. No ironing needed, ever.
fabrics.press: Press seams lightly; don't flatten the puckers
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry.
tips: Match the stripes at side seams by lining up the pattern pieces on the same stripe.

fabrics.name: Linen
fabrics.drape: Crisp at first, softens with washing
fabrics.about: Strong, cool, and gets softer every wash. It wrinkles easily, and that's part of its charm.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and tumble dry, twice if you want it soft. It can shrink 5% or more.
tips: Linen frays a lot, so finish seams right after sewing them.
Pull a thread to find a straight cut line.

fabrics.name: Linen-cotton blend
fabrics.about: The look of linen with fewer wrinkles and a softer hand from the cotton. Often cheaper than pure linen.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry.
tips: A forgiving first 'nice' fabric for a garment.

fabrics.name: Wool flannel
fabrics.about: A soft, slightly fuzzy wool for tailored clothes. Shapes beautifully with steam.
fabrics.press: Medium (wool setting) with steam and always a pressing cloth
fabrics.prewash: Steam the whole piece with an iron held just above it, or take it to a dry cleaner. Don't machine wash.
tips: Let pressed wool cool flat before moving it: that's when the shape sets.
Use a clapper (a wooden block) to get flat seams.

fabrics.name: Wool crepe
fabrics.stretch: A little, from the twisted yarns
fabrics.about: Made with tightly twisted yarns that give a pebbly texture and lovely drape. Barely wrinkles.
fabrics.press: Medium with steam and a pressing cloth
fabrics.prewash: Steam well before cutting, or dry clean.
tips: Staystitch necklines: crepe can stretch out of shape.

fabrics.name: Wool coating
fabrics.fiber: Wool, often with nylon or cashmere
fabrics.about: Thick and warm, often felted on the surface (like melton). Hard to fray, but bulky.
fabrics.press: Medium with steam, a pressing cloth, and a clapper
fabrics.prewash: Steam well before cutting, or dry clean.
tips: Grade (trim to different widths) seam allowances to cut down bulk.
Cut one layer at a time if it's very thick.

fabrics.name: Silk charmeuse
fabrics.about: Glossy on the front and dull on the back, with a liquid drape. Beautiful and slippery.
fabrics.press: Low (silk setting), from the wrong side, with a silk organza pressing cloth. Steam can spot it.
fabrics.prewash: Hand wash cool if you'll hand wash the garment; otherwise dry clean.
tips: Cut it between two layers of tissue paper so it doesn't slide.
Use very fine pins only inside the seam allowance: holes show.

fabrics.name: Crepe de chine
fabrics.about: Matte with a soft, slightly pebbly texture. A little easier to handle than charmeuse.
fabrics.prewash: Hand wash cool, or dry clean.
tips: French seams look beautiful on it.

fabrics.name: Silk dupioni
fabrics.about: Crisp silk with irregular slubs (little thick spots) and a rich shimmer. Holds a shape well.
fabrics.press: Low to medium, dry, with a pressing cloth. Water spots it.
fabrics.prewash: Dry clean. Washing changes its crisp hand.
tips: Frays a lot, so finish seams right away.
Underline it with cotton batiste for structure.

fabrics.name: Rayon challis
fabrics.about: Soft, swishy, and cool, made from wood pulp. Drapes like silk for a fraction of the price, but it moves while you cut.
fabrics.press: Medium, from the wrong side, with a pressing cloth
fabrics.prewash: Wash cool and hang to dry, the same way you'll wash the garment. It can shrink 5–10%.
tips: Lay it flat and smooth it on grain before cutting: it twists easily.
Pattern weights and a rotary cutter beat pins and shears here.

fabrics.name: Viscose crepe
fabrics.about: A crepe texture in viscose: matte, drapey, and less slippery than challis.
fabrics.prewash: Hand wash cool, hang to dry.
tips: Staystitch curves right after cutting.

fabrics.name: Tencel twill
fabrics.about: A wood-pulp fiber like rayon, but stronger when wet. Often sanded so it feels like suede. Drapes beautifully.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash gentle, tumble dry low or hang.
tips: Pressing too hot leaves shiny marks: test on a scrap.

fabrics.name: Polyester crepe and georgette
fabrics.about: Doesn't wrinkle and washes easily. Georgette is sheer and springy; crepe is opaque. Doesn't breathe like natural fibers.
fabrics.press: Low (synthetic setting), with a pressing cloth. Too hot melts it.
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash cool. It barely shrinks.
tips: Polyester resists creases, so press seams firmly and let them cool.

fabrics.name: Chiffon
fabrics.about: Sheer, floaty, and slippery. Gorgeous as an overlayer, tricky to cut and sew.
fabrics.prewash: Hand wash cool if washable.
tips: Cut between tissue paper.
Start seams on a scrap of tissue paper and tear it away after, so the needle doesn't eat the fabric.

fabrics.name: Polyester satin
fabrics.about: Shiny on the front and dull on the back, with long floating threads. Snags easily.
fabrics.press: Low, from the wrong side, with a pressing cloth
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash cool if the garment will be washed.
tips: Watch for snagged rings or rough fingers.
The shine changes with direction: cut all pieces the same way up.

fabrics.name: Cotton jersey
fabrics.stretch: Across the width, often 30–50%; more with spandex
fabrics.about: T-shirt fabric: smooth knit stitches on the front, little loops on the back. The edges curl when cut.
fabrics.stitch: A narrow zigzag or your machine's stretch stitch
fabrics.press: Medium, pressing, not sliding, so it doesn't stretch
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry. Cotton jersey shrinks.
tips: Knits get their own level (9): try jersey after that.
Lay the stretch going around the body.
Starch the curly edges flat before sewing.

fabrics.name: Rib knit
fabrics.stretch: Very stretchy across, with great recovery
fabrics.about: Raised vertical ribs on both sides, so it stretches a lot and springs back. Doesn't curl.
fabrics.stitch: A narrow zigzag or stretch stitch
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry.
tips: Neckbands are cut shorter than the neckline and stretched to fit, which makes them lie flat.

fabrics.name: French terry
fabrics.about: Smooth knit on the front, soft little loops on the back. Comfy, stable, and easy to sew for a knit.
fabrics.stitch: A narrow zigzag or stretch stitch
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry.
tips: Pair it with rib knit for cuffs and waistbands.

fabrics.name: Sweatshirt fleece
fabrics.about: Like French terry, but the back is brushed into a fuzzy layer. Warm and cozy.
fabrics.stitch: A narrow zigzag or stretch stitch
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash and dry.
tips: Lints a lot: clean your machine after.

fabrics.name: Ponte
fabrics.about: A thick, stable double knit that looks the same on both sides and doesn't curl. The easiest knit to start with.
fabrics.stitch: A narrow zigzag or stretch stitch
fabrics.press: Low to medium, with a pressing cloth
fabrics.prewash: Machine wash cool, dry low.
tips: Because it barely curls, it's good for a first knit project.
